How it works

  • Exact match. The key is a hash of the route, model, the calling key (when isolated) and the full request body with keys sorted — any change to messages or parameters is a different entry.
  • Cached: non-streaming chat completions, completions, embeddings, rerank and score.
  • Never cached: streaming requests, requests with n > 1, the stateful responses API, and errors.
  • Temperature is not considered. A hit replays the earlier sample even at temperature > 0; send Cache-Control: no-cache when you need a fresh one.
  • Hits still pass authentication, budget and rate-limit checks and pre-call guardrails, then are logged as cache_hit with a cost of $0.
  • The cache lives in memory of each LemonGate instance: it is empty after a restart and not shared between replicas.
Per-request control
Cache-Control: no-cacheSkip the lookup and call the model; the fresh response is still stored.
Cache-Control: no-storeUse a cached response if present, but do not store this one.
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-storeBypass the cache entirely.
x-lemongate-cache-ttl: 3600Store this response for N seconds instead of the default (max 24 h).
x-lemongate-cache: hit | missResponse header telling you whether the cache answered.
 
curl -i {{.BaseURL}}/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LEMONGATE_KEY" \
  -H "x-lemongate-cache-ttl: 3600" \
  -d '{"model": "MODEL", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]}'
x-lemongate-cache: hit
{{end}} {{end}}
